sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface localization confirmed by use in surface expression studies (L1); construct used for cell-surface co-expression and signalling assays (L4). Kinase activity of the tagged receptor was NOT MEASURED explicitly in either paper.
sites.rationale: Both L1 and L4 report N-terminal epitope tags on full-length, membrane-anchored EphB4 used for surface-expression studies, establishing that the extracellular N-terminus tolerates a short tag. The signal peptide spans residues 1–15 (landmark-authoritative); any N-terminal tag must be placed after cleavage, i.e., after residue 15 (A) and before residue 16 (L), the mature N-terminus. Python confirms seq[14]='A' and seq[15]='L'. No residue is named in either paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived: with a single-pass type-I topology and a 525-residue extracellular domain, the post-signal-peptide N-terminus is the only extracellular N-terminal junction available. L1 (PMC9795039): HA epitope tag engineered at the NH2-terminus of full-length EphB4 in a lentiviral expression construct for surface expression studies; the construct is full-length and membrane-anchored. Corroborated by L4 (PMC10168364), which places an N-terminal HA leader + c-myc tag + GSPGGA linker on full-length EphB4 in pCEP4 for surface expression studies. Neither paper names a specific residue; the signal peptide (residues 1–15) is cleaved, so the only extracellular N-terminal junction is after residue 15 (A) and before residue 16 (L), the mature N-terminus.

sources.claim: HA and flag epitopes were tagged at the NH2-terminus of EphB4 and ephrinB2, respectively, and GFP was fused to the NH2-terminus of ephrinB2.

literature_notes: L1 and L4 both ground the same N-terminal junction (after residue 15) on full-length EphB4; they are treated as one site with L1 as the primary clip and L4 as corroboration. L2 and L3 (PMC13270174) report a C-terminal eGFP fusion confirmed at the plasma membrane by immunofluorescence, but the C-terminus (residue 987) falls within the intracellular domain (topology landmarks: intracellular 562–987); this tag is therefore placed in other_positions as intracellular. No ledger line reports any insertion in an internal extracellular loop of EphB4, so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal eGFP fusion (EphB4-eGFP) confirmed at the plasma membrane by immunofluorescence in 22Rv1 cells, but residue 987 lies within the intracellular kinase domain (topology 562–987); the tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
